newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Merck prices AIDS drug in Ecus.
newsitem.headline: Merck prices AIDS drug in Ecus.

text.p: Pharmaceutical company Merck said it was pricing its anti-AIDS drug Crixivan, approved for the European Union market on Friday, in European currency units.

The company said in a statement Crixivan was the first pharmaceutical product to use that pricing strategy. It has set the price for a day's supply of Crixivan at 9.64 Ecus -- equivalent to the global price of $12.
"Previously (Merck) had targeted a single, U.S.-dollar denominated price in Europe for its products," the statement said.
"However, exchange rate fluctuations and other factors can adversely affect the price, and thereby the availability, of products."
The Ecu price will be converted into local currency equivalents during discussions with national authorities for final local pricing and government reimbursement approvals, it said.
The European Commission approved Crixivan for sale across the 15-member EU on Friday, acting on the advice of the European Medicines Evaluation Agency in London. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
